pNone_chapter_1: In a sun-drenched colonial-era living room in Kolkata, Byomkesh Bakshi sits reclined in a wooden armchair, his lean frame draped in a white dhoti-kurta as he meticulously scrutinizes a sprawling newspaper. Beside him, Ajit Bandyopadhyay leans over a small round table, holding a steaming clay cup of tea while looking toward his friend with an expectant expression. Dust motes dance in the warm morning light filtering through tall slatted windows, illuminating the floor-to-ceiling bookshelves that line the background. A thin trail of smoke rises from a cigarette resting in an ashtray, adding to the quiet, contemplative atmosphere of the domestic setting.
